target_customer: Systems engineering teams at aerospace, defense, robotics, energy and automotive companies, from startups to large organizations
problem: Engineering teams building complex hardware keep requirements, architecture, analysis and tests in silos and in heavy legacy MBSE tools, which slows iteration and hurts alignment.
product_category: AI-native model-based systems engineering software (SysML v2)

founders.name: Sebastian Völkl
prior_employers: European Space Agency project (Moon greenhouse module modeling)
founders.background_notes: From YC page; education not listed.

founders.name: Eliot Khachi
founders.background_notes: Systems integration and test engineer who planned tests for a navy propulsion system; calls himself an autodidact. Quit his job in spring 2024 per the company description.

competitors.name: Cameo Systems Modeler (Dassault Systemes)
competitors.traction_then: long standing incumbent tool, quote-only pricing

competitors.name: Innoslate (SPEC Innovations)
competitors.what: Browser based requirements and MBSE platform
competitors.traction_then: established, used in a Defense Acquisition University pilot

technical_complexity.rationale: A SysML v2 model with traceability, analysis hooks and an LLM copilot over engineering documents is demanding domain engineering, though not research grade.

defensibility.rationale: Once a program's requirements and architecture live in a model, migration is costly, and defense and aerospace buyers value domain credibility; incumbents hold the installed base.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent tools persist and AI features are being added to engineering suites; no acquisition of Dalus found.

market_need_then: Aerospace and defense programs were adopting model-based systems engineering and the founder lived the silo problem at Aerojet; a design partner named in company materials was Israel Aerospace Industries.

identity.logo: DALUS wordmark with a logo mark
identity.voice_and_tone: The MBSE platform your engineers will actually use

branding.community_and_virality: A founder post launching the beta on r/systems_engineering in January 2025; no evidence of merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Niche B2B audience and little brand coverage; name is close to Daedalus and DalusAI, an Israeli construction startup.

outcome_analysis: Dalus is active with a three person team in San Francisco. An ex Aerojet engineer and a serial hardware founder launched a cheaper cloud MBSE tool in early 2025, joined YC in Winter 2025 and report defense customers such as DefendTex. Funding is not confirmed, so the trajectory beyond early traction is unknown.
notes: Caplight lists a seed round of undisclosed size dated March 2025 (total 600K by one reading) and Startup Seeker estimates 500K; Getlatka lists 0. All are aggregators, so no round is recorded. Getlatka revenue estimate of 330K for 2025 is unverified. Name origin not found. Customer logos DefendTex and IOX Lab from the company site. Completeness pass: the March 2025 seed rests on a single database (Origami) with amount undisclosed; Startup Seeker says about $500K and Caplight $600K total, so the amount is left null. No press announcement found.
